                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">There are specific provisions e.g. in the general policies, rules and regulations of the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In signing the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, the institution agrees to respect <strong>in full</strong> the principles of non-discrimination as set out in the Programme. The institution must clearly demonstrate through its policies, rules and regulations that equal access and opportunities to mobile participants from all backgrounds. Which means that all individuals or groups will be treated equally, irrespective of their characteristics. In accordance with Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, there should be no discrimination "based on sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation". For more information, see: <a href="http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf">http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The principle - that extra fees are not being charged to incoming mobile students - is implemented</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The receiving institution must <strong>not </strong>charge any type of fees to incoming mobility students for the tuition, registration or examination of these students or for their access to laboratory, library and other facilities offered to local students.<br>In certain cases, however, mobile students may be required to pay small fees for insurance, student unions, use of miscellaneous materials (e.g. photocopies, laboratory products) on the same basis as these are charged to local students. Students should be made aware of these extra costs before the start of mobility. Fees may only be charged in the case of full degree mobility or for students registered in joint degree programmes.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All students and staff (incoming and outgoing) are treated equally in all academic and service matters</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In accordance with equal access and opportunities, all students and staff should be treated equally in all academic and service matters. Clear appeal procedures should be in place to ensure equal treatment. There should be individuals - such as mentors and counsellors - available to offer support.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It provides incoming mobile participants with access to the same services and facilities available to local students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is vital to ensure that incoming mobility participants have full access to the same services and facilities as local students and staff. For example, mobility participants with special needs can benefit from the support services that the receiving institution offers to its local students and staff.</p>                      </div>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That is up-to-date, ECTS based and available on the institution's website</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important for each HEI to produce an online Course Catalogue, which includes detailed, user-friendly and up-to-date information on the institution’s educational offer and learning environment to enable students to make the right choices and use their time most efficiently, before and during their study period. The Course Catalogue should follow the guidelines set out in the ECTS Users' Guide (http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm) to increase comparability and transparency. It should be published on the institution's website sufficiently in advance i.e. to enable prospective mobile students to make their choices.</p><p>It should include general information on the institution, its resources and services, as well as academic information on its programmes and individual educational components. The ECTS Users' Guide recommends using the following common structure:</p><ul><li>General information</li><li>Resources and services</li><li>Information on study programmes</li><li>Information on single course units</li></ul><p>The Course Catalogue should also include the names of people to contact, with information about how, when and where to contact them.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That is updated regularly and sufficiently in advance for prospective mobile students to make their choices</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>

                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The purpose of the Learning Agreement is to provide a transparent and efficient preparation of the study period abroad and to ensure that the student will receive recognition in his/her degree for the educational components or traineeship successfully completed abroad. The Learning Agreement:</p><ul><li>Sets out the learning outcomes for the mobility, including both the educational components or traineeship activities to be carried out by the student at the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise, which will be recognised by the sending institution upon successful completion of the study programme abroad and counted towards his/her degree.</li><li>Ensures full recognition for satisfactorily completed activities of study mobility and traineeships in terms of credits awarded, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams, and documents these credits in the student records, so that they can be identified in a transparent way.</li></ul><p>The Learning Agreement is binding for all parties and constitutes the cornerstone of successful student mobility (for studies, traineeships, and combinations thereof), including quality assurances and the process for transparent transfer of credits. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>

                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>

                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI

Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.

For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.

Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.

You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

 
 

The role

Data at Langdock sits close to Product Development because our product is our core business. Understanding how people use Langdock requires detailed product context, especially as the product evolves quickly and raw events can be easy to misinterpret.

As our first dedicated data hire, you will own the path from raw data to trusted decisions. You will sit between product and engineering, combining data engineering, analytics engineering, product analytics, and technical platform ownership.

You will not start from scratch. We already run the dbt transformation framework on ClickHouse, ingest product, billing, and customer data, and provide business-facing marts and Metabase dashboards. Your role is to turn these foundations into a reliable data system that the company can trust and build on.

 

What you will own

  • Make company metrics trustworthy. Define and model metrics so people understand what each number means, how it is calculated, and where its limitations are. Resolve inconsistencies and prevent teams from working with conflicting definitions.

  • Build a reliable model of product usage. Develop a deep understanding of Langdock's products and translate raw application data into useful models for activation, adoption, retention, feature usage, and customer health.

  • Own the data platform in production. Build and operate ingestion pipelines, warehouse models, data quality checks, deployment workflows, and monitoring. Ensure that data remains accurate, fresh, observable, and available when people depend on it.

  • Partner with Product Engineers. Help product squads understand how people use what they build, answer exploratory questions, evaluate product changes, and identify opportunities or problems that are not obvious from individual customer conversations.

  • Improve product instrumentation. Find blind spots in the data we collect and work with engineers to design events and source data that make future analysis reliable.

  • Serve the company's core data consumers. Enable Account Management to understand adoption within specific accounts, help Revenue and Finance understand where the company makes money, and provide leadership with dependable company-level reporting.

  • Create self-service foundations. Build clear marts, documentation, and dashboards that let teams answer recurring questions without requiring a custom analysis each time.

 

What makes this role different

This is neither a dashboard-only analytics role nor an infrastructure-only data engineering role. You will own the complete system, from how product data is generated to how a metric is interpreted in a product or business decision.

The hardest part is not writing SQL or operating ClickHouse. It is developing enough product and business context to model ambiguous data correctly while building technical systems that remain dependable as Langdock changes quickly.

Because this is our first dedicated data hire, you will establish the standards for data modeling, quality, ownership, observability, and collaboration across Product Development.

 

What success could look like

Within your first year:

  • Product, Account Management, RevOps, and leadership use consistent definitions for the company's most important metrics.

  • Product squads can understand adoption and behavior without questioning whether the underlying data is correct.

  • Important pipelines and models have explicit owners, tests, freshness expectations, monitoring, and recovery procedures.

  • Gaps in product instrumentation are identified and addressed as part of product development.

  • Recurring questions are answered through reusable models and dashboards rather than one-off queries.

  • The company has a clear technical direction for how the data platform should evolve.

 

What we are looking for

  • You have built and operated production data pipelines and analytical models, not only consumed data prepared by others.

  • You can move between infrastructure, SQL modeling, exploratory analysis, and conversations about product or business definitions.

  • You treat data quality and metric definitions as product responsibilities.

  • You are comfortable working with dbt, analytical databases, deployment systems, and business intelligence tools.

  • You investigate surprising numbers until you understand the underlying product behavior and technical mechanism.

  • You can turn an ambiguous question into a clear definition, a dependable model, and an actionable explanation.

  • You want broad ownership and are motivated by establishing the foundations for a growing data function.

 

Working here

This is an in-office role at Greifswalder Strasse 212 in Berlin. We work together in person because it helps us build trust, develop shared context, and make decisions quickly.

Most engineers start around 8:30. We usually eat lunch together, and dinner is available for people who stay later. Running and gym are part of the routine for many of us.

You need an existing right to work in Germany. We do not currently sponsor visas.

 

Compensation

The salary range for this role is €90,000–€140,000 gross per year, depending on level and scope. All roles include equity. Salaries are tied to levels, not negotiation.

We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience.

 

Compensation: €90K – €140K • Offers Equity

Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe's largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

 

About Langdock

Our mission is to bridge the gap between technology and adoption. We build a secure, model-agnostic AI platform that helps companies put AI to work across their entire organisation. From chat and agents to integrations, workflows, and our API, we give teams the tools to augment and automate their work.

We apply the same ambition internally. We want to be the most productive company in the world, and that means continuously improving how we work, not simply adding more people to existing processes.

 

About the Role

Thousands of small teams already pay for Langdock. They found us on their own, without any marketing aimed at them and without a single euro spent on ads. We are building a dedicated growth team to turn that into a deliberate engine, and you will be the person who brings those teams in.

You decide where our acquisition time and money go: the website, comparison pages, organic search, paid, partnerships, and whatever we haven't tried yet. You run it yourself, and you're accountable for the results.

This is a builder role. You and our growth engineer decide what to build. You run the experiment, read the data, and decide what to scale or kill.

You'll join a small growth team that reports directly to our co-CEO, Lennard:

  • a growth engineer who builds the product side of experiments

  • a growth activation lead who turns new signups into active users

 

What you will do

  • Own the self-serve funnel. From first visit to paying team: the website, signup, pricing, and converting free users into paying ones.

  • Run experiments. Paid, organic, partnerships, new markets. Set budgets and kill criteria before spending, and judge results.

  • Write the copy. Landing pages, comparison pages, ad variants, in-product messages. You build drafts for everything you test; our growth engineer translates them into production.

 

What we are looking for

  • You are a heavy user of AI in your daily work, with opinions on what works and what does not. We are looking for people who are already compounding their output with AI.

  • You have owned acquisition across channels. You have been accountable for a full acquisition number, and you can talk about the numbers.

  • You're hands-on, with depth and range. You're an expert in at least one channel, capable across the rest, and happy to do the work yourself.

  • You are close to the product. You can understand a platform like ours well enough to explain it to small teams, and you work well with engineers.

  • You are experiments-driven and comfortable with data. Cohorts, CAC and payback are familiar ground, and you pull your own numbers.

  • You are a kind person who cares about the people around you.

  • Nice to have: experience at a product-led company that later added enterprise sales, localised go-to-market in European markets.

  • Localisation is an important part of the job. You have run campaigns in more than one market, and you are comfortable adapting messaging and pages for a new language.

 

Our Values

  • Calm urgency. We move fast without chaos. We stay calm, fix what matters, and avoid unnecessary noise. We focus on solutions rather than complaints and make sure sleep, health, and sports keep our decision-making sharp.

  • Ambitious execution. We love building fast and with ownership. We aim to be the most productive company in the world. Learning, shipping, and improving bring us joy. Everyone is expected to ask questions, take initiative, and deliver reliably.

  • Caring ownership. We care deeply: about each other, customers, and the world around us. We act with empathy, sincerity, and long-term thinking. And we have fun along the way while spending time in the office together.

 

The Environment

We work from our office in Berlin, Greifswalder Strasse 212. Everyone works together in person because the hardest problems get solved faster at a whiteboard than in a Slack thread. Conversations happen faster, problems get solved quicker, and we actually know each other.

Days start at 8:30. Lunch and dinner are catered in the office. We run, go to the gym, and take care of ourselves. Health is not separate from work here, it is part of how we work well.

The vibe is calm but intense. No one is yelling or panicking. But everyone is working hard on things that matter.

 

Compensation

All roles include equity. We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience. We narrow down the expected salary range early in the process.

 

When you apply

We would love to see two short examples: one channel you built or scaled, and one experiment you ran that changed a conversion rate. Tell us what you owned, the numbers, and what you would do differently. That counts for more than your CV.

 

Next steps

We move fast. Most processes complete within two weeks.

If this sounds like your kind of work, we would like to meet you.

    About Zelara

    Most CRM marketing still blasts generic messages at scale and calls it "personalization." Our founders experienced this firsthand in senior roles at HelloFresh, Salesforce, Uber, and others. Backed by top-tier VCs, they decided to build a better way.

    Zelara is an agentic lifecycle marketing platform that improves with every interaction. It works with the CRM infrastructure our customers already use, replacing static journeys and manual segmentation with a system that creates content, makes individual-level decisions, and learns from every outcome.

    With bunq, Europe's second-largest neobank, we delivered +7.4% activation and +66% reactivation uplift, measured against a control group. We raised a €3M pre-seed and are generating revenue with paying enterprise customers. Our founders still run the commercial side themselves. We are hiring the person who takes that over and turns it into a motion that does not depend on them.

    The Role

    This is not a role where you inherit a mature sales organisation and work a territory. Leads do not arrive from marketing, opportunities do not arrive from SDRs, and there is no playbook written by someone else for you to run.

    This is a hands-on senior AE role: you carry a number and close your own deals. You own the commercial motion end-to-end at the moment it stops being founder-led: the pitch lands, the workshops work, paying customers are signing, and none of it is yet a system that someone other than a founder can repeat.

    You own the full funnel, from identifying who is worth talking to through discovery, workshop, offer, negotiation, and signature, and on into the annual contract, expansion, and renewal. Annual contracts run €75–250k. Cycles run two to four months. Buying committees are a CRM champion, a technical stakeholder, and an economic buyer, and you need to know why each of them says no.

    You and the Solutions Architect run each account as a pair, in a weekly rhythm and in the room together for the conversations that decide something. You are the account owner: pricing, proposals, contracts, conversion to an annual contract, expansion, renewal. They own the technical plan and the evidence behind those decisions. Before signature they lead technical discovery alongside you; after signature they become the customer's named technical lead. You close; they make the value real and defensible.

    You will sell to CRM, lifecycle, and marketing leaders at mid-market and enterprise B2C companies across Europe: fintech, e-commerce, travel, and employee benefits.

    • Own the full funnel from ICP identification to signed contract: source, qualify, run discovery, facilitate workshops, write offers, negotiate, and close

    • Close the next wave of customers alongside a founder, then without one, and turn closing from a personal skill into a system someone else can run

    • Win the build-versus-buy conversation: prepare it with the Solutions Architect, bring the evidence, and make the case to an engineering lead who would rather build it

    • Turn a working pitch into a documented playbook: write down what wins, retire what does not, and make the next hire productive from it

    • Run outbound as an experiment rather than a spray: test channels, messaging, and segments with a stated hypothesis and a result you are willing to act on

    • Shape ICP and positioning with real market signal, and feed what you hear in deals back to Product and Science rather than storing it in your head

    • Build the commercial foundation: pricing logic, contract mechanics, pipeline hygiene, and a forecast that holds up

    • Own the commercial side of expansion and renewal with the Solutions Architect: identify the opportunity, quantify the value, and de-risk the plan

    • Lead sales as the team grows: once the motion is repeatable, hire and coach the next account executives

    • Act with Integrity: We build trust through transparency, reliability, and ownership.

    • Put Customers First: We succeed only when they succeed.

    • Accelerate Impact: We prefer speed, simplicity, and real learning over ceremony.

    About Zip

    Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

    The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

    Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

    Your Role

    You'll be a force multiplier for the Pre-sales organization. You'll own how Zip demos end to end: the environments, data, scripts, and certification standards that let any Solution Engineer deliver a technically credible demo quickly and consistently. You will be responsible for developing the solution demo frameworks, reusable assets, and self-service approach that every Solution Engineer and Account Executive benefits from.

    You’ll work closely with Solution Engineering leadership, Enterprise Architecture, Product, and Product Marketing to design our demos of the future. This is a hands-on builder role, not a maintenance seat. You're building the systems and vision for what a great demo looks like at Zip.

    What You'll Do

    • Own demo environment build and operations: Design, build, and maintain the demo environments, data sets, demo pathways, and demo scripts every SEs uses.

    • Build self-service tooling and templates: Turn demo-builds into packages assets that SEs and AEs can pull directly.

    • Shape our demo narratives and storytelling: Develop the talk tracks, narrative arcs, and messaging that turn technical features into a story every SE can tell.

    • Keep demo assets in lockstep with releases: Partner with Product and Product Marketing so new agents, integrations, and vertical use cases ship with a working demo environment and script.

    • Automate scripting and asset generation with AI: Use LLMs and AI coding tools to generate and maintain demo scripts, synthetic data, and environment scaffolding, cutting manual build time on every new demo asset.

    • Automate end-to-end demo workflows with Playwright: Script and maintain Playwright-based flows that walk through full demo scenarios automatically, so environments get validated and refreshed without manual QA.

    • Build with AI-native development tools: Prototype and ship internal tooling using tools like Replit and Lovable, taking new demo assets from idea to working build.

    • Build and maintain agentic loops: Design agent workflows that can prepare, validate, and repair demo environments on their own, catching broken flows before an SE does.

    Qualifications

    • 2–5+ years in technical pre-sales, sales engineering, or demo engineering at a high-growth B2B SaaS company.

    • Real hands-on build skills: scripting fluency (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar), comfort with REST APIs and webhooks, and enough cloud/infrastructure familiarity (AWS, GCP, or Azure) to stand up and operate a demo environment without waiting on engineering.

    • Hands-on experience using AI to automate scripting and asset generation

    • Experience automating end-to-end workflows with Playwright or a comparable browser-automation framework, for demo environment validation, regression testing, or scripted walkthroughs.

    • Direct experience building with AI-native development tools such as Replit, Lovable, or similar. Comfortable going from a blank canvas to a working prototype largely through AI-assisted building.

    • Experience designing and maintaining agentic loops: multi-step AI agent workflows that execute, evaluate, and self-correct.

    • A systems thinker who can tell the difference between fixing the one-off request in front of them and building the thing that prevents the next ten.

    • Strong storytelling instincts: you know the difference between a feature tour and a demo that lands, and you can teach that difference to other people.

    • A strong cross-functional operator: you'll work daily with SE leadership, Product, PMM, and Enterprise Architecture, and you know how to get alignment without a committee.

    Nice to have

    • Experience selling into procurement, finance, or supply chain functions.

    • Familiarity with ERP and enterprise systems (SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite, ServiceNow) and how they intersect with procurement technology, for cross-system demo integrations.

    Perks & Benefits

    At Zip, we’re committed to providing our employees with everything they need to do their best work.

    • 📈 Start-up equity

    • 🦷 Health, vision & dental coverage

    • Commuter benefit

    • 🌴 Flexible PTO

    • 💻 Apple equipment plus home office stipend

    • 5% Employer Pension Contribution

    About Pleo

    Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

    The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

    Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

    About the role

    We’re looking for a Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager to join our Customer Experience team at Pleo. In this role, you’ll own a portfolio of large, complex, and strategically important enterprise customers, helping them achieve measurable business outcomes, expand adoption, manage change, and build long-term value with Pleo.

    You’ll serve as a trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders while coordinating the broader Pleo relationship across Customer Success, Product, Support, Sales, Finance, and other internal teams.

    This is not a reactive account-management role. You’ll be expected to understand each customer’s business priorities, operating model, success criteria, and risk profile. You’ll turn that understanding into clear success plans, executive engagement strategies, adoption programs, renewal plans, and growth opportunities.

    The right candidate will bring at least three years of direct experience managing enterprise customers, along with the communication skills, commercial judgment, and operational discipline required to manage high-value relationships in a fast-paced technology environment.

    Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

    You’ll report to our Manager of Customer Success, Large & High-Growth Customers and work closely with teams across:

    • Customer Support

    • Customer Onboarding

    • Sales and Account Management

    • Product and Product Operations

    • Revenue Operations

    • Finance

    • Data and Analytics

    • Program Management and Operations

    You’ll work with customer stakeholders across finance, procurement, operations, technology, transformation, and executive leadership.

    You’ll be responsible for creating alignment across these stakeholders, establishing clear governance, and ensuring Pleo remains connected to the customer’s evolving strategic and operational priorities.

    What you’ll be doing

    As a Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager, you will:

    • Own a portfolio of enterprise customers with accountability for customer health, value realisation, adoption, retention, renewal readiness, advocacy, and growth.

    • Build trusted relationships with senior and executive stakeholders, positioning yourself as a credible advisor who understands their business priorities and operating environment.

    • Develop detailed customer success plans that connect the customer’s strategic goals to measurable outcomes, adoption milestones, responsibilities, and timelines.

    • Lead executive business reviews and strategic customer meetings that demonstrate value, address risks, align stakeholders, and create clear next steps.

    • Drive product adoption across complex customer organisations, helping customers expand usage across teams, entities, locations, use cases, and workflows.

    • Create and maintain detailed stakeholder maps, identifying decision-makers, champions, influencers, operational contacts, blockers, and executive sponsors.

    • Identify churn risk early using product usage, engagement, stakeholder, support, financial, organisational, and external business signals.

    • Build and execute churn-prevention plans with clear actions, owners, timelines, customer commitments, and executive escalation paths.

    • Maintain detailed and accurate forecasts across renewals, risk, customer health, expected outcomes, growth opportunities, and major account milestones.

    • Lead renewal-readiness activities by ensuring customer value is documented, risks are addressed, stakeholders are aligned, and commercial partners have accurate account intelligence.

    • Identify and support expansion opportunities by connecting additional Pleo capabilities, products, or use cases to the customer’s evolving business needs.

    • Coordinate complex customer escalations across Support, Product, Engineering, Finance, and other teams while maintaining clear and confident customer communication.

    • Act as the customer’s internal advocate, ensuring customer needs, feedback, risks, and opportunities are visible to the right stakeholders at Pleo.

    • Navigate customer change effectively, including leadership transitions, reorganisations, acquisitions, market expansion, platform changes, and evolving business priorities.

    • Track customer commitments and outcomes with strong operational discipline, ensuring actions are documented, owned, and completed.

    • Contribute to the evolution of Pleo’s enterprise Customer Success model by sharing best practices, customer insights, playbooks, and recommendations.

    • Support peer development and knowledge sharing across the Customer Success team without holding direct people-management responsibility.

    To put things into context

    In this role, you can expect to work on priorities such as:

    • strengthening relationships with Pleo’s largest and most strategic customers

    • improving enterprise customer retention and renewal predictability

    • increasing adoption across complex customer organisations

    • creating stronger executive engagement and governance

    • identifying churn risk before it becomes a renewal issue

    • improving forecast accuracy and account visibility

    • coordinating complex customer needs across multiple internal teams

    • helping customers quantify and communicate the value they receive from Pleo

    • identifying opportunities for expansion and deeper product adoption

    • improving the consistency and quality of enterprise success planning

    • helping customers navigate operational and organisational change

    • turning customer feedback into actionable Product and CX insight

    You can expect to work across a technology environment that includes CRM, Customer Success platforms, support systems, product analytics, business intelligence tools, workflow tools, and collaboration platforms.

    Examples may include Vitally, Gainsight or similar, Zendesk, Looker, Tableau or Power BI, Jira, Asana, and Slack.

    What you bring

    You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

    • At least three years of direct enterprise Customer Success or strategic account-management experience, managing large, complex, and high-value B2B customers.

    • Five or more years of overall experience in Customer Success, account management, consulting, implementation, or a related customer-facing role.

    • Experience working in SaaS, fintech, enterprise technology, or another complex B2B technology environment.

    • A proven record of retaining and growing enterprise customers, including managing renewals, adoption, risk, and value realisation.

    • Strong executive relationship-management skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage senior decision-makers and business leaders.

    • Experience managing complex stakeholder environments involving multiple teams, business units, regions, entities, or decision-makers.

    • Strong churn-prediction and prevention skills, including the ability to interpret customer signals, identify root causes, and build effective recovery plans.

    • Detailed forecasting experience across renewals, customer risk, account health, adoption, and expansion opportunities.

    • Strong commercial judgment, with an understanding of how customer outcomes connect to retention, revenue, expansion, and long-term account value.

    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to lead difficult conversations, present to executives, and simplify complex issues.

    • Experience building strategic success plans, account plans, stakeholder maps, and executive business reviews.

    • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret customer data, product usage, service trends, and business information.

    • Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to align internal stakeholders without relying on direct authority.

    • A structured and proactive approach to account management, with excellent follow-through and attention to detail.

    • Comfort working in a fast-paced growth environment where customer expectations, internal priorities, and business needs can evolve quickly.

    • The ability to balance strategic relationship management with detailed operational execution.

    Nice to have

    • Experience in fintech, payments, spend management, financial operations, or expense-management technology

    • Experience working with finance leaders, procurement teams, controllers, CFO organisations, or transformation leaders

    • Experience managing multi-country or multinational enterprise customers

    • Familiarity with ERP, accounting, procurement, or financial-system integrations

    • Experience supporting customers through significant organisational or technology transformation

    • Exposure to AI-enabled Customer Success, predictive health models, automated risk detection, or digital engagement

    • Experience partnering with Product teams on strategic customer feedback and roadmap discussions

    • Experience managing accounts with complex security, compliance, governance, or implementation requirements

    Why is this role a good fit for you?

    This role is a good fit for you if:

    • You enjoy building strategic relationships with complex enterprise customers.

    • You are comfortable engaging senior leaders and navigating high-stakes customer situations.

    • You know how to connect product adoption to measurable customer outcomes.

    • You are proactive about identifying and addressing churn risk.

    • You combine strong relationship skills with rigorous account-management discipline.

    • You are confident leading executive reviews, renewal discussions, and difficult customer conversations.

    • You enjoy coordinating internal teams around complex customer needs.

    • You want direct responsibility for protecting and growing some of Pleo’s most important customer relationships.

    This role is not a good fit for you if:

    • You have not directly managed enterprise or strategic customer relationships.

    • You prefer transactional or high-volume customer portfolios.

    • You are uncomfortable owning customer risk, retention, and renewal readiness.

    • You prefer reacting to customer requests rather than building proactive engagement strategies.

    • You are uncomfortable engaging executive stakeholders or leading difficult conversations.

    • You do not enjoy detailed forecasting, CRM management, and account planning.

    • You prefer working independently without significant cross-functional coordination.

    • You are looking for a people-management role rather than a senior individual-contributor position.

    How you’ll develop in this role

    In your first 1 month at Pleo, you’ll:

    • Learn Pleo’s product, enterprise customer journey, value proposition, and Customer Success operating model.

    • Build a detailed understanding of your customer portfolio, including revenue, renewal dates, usage, stakeholders, open issues, risks, and growth potential.

    • Establish relationships with key customer stakeholders and internal account partners.

    • Review and improve success plans, stakeholder maps, account plans, and risk assessments.

    • Establish clear operating rhythms for customer engagement, internal coordination, and forecasting.

    • Identify immediate risks, adoption gaps, and opportunities across your portfolio.

    In your first 3 months, you’ll:

    • Lead consistent executive and operational engagement across your customer portfolio.

    • Improve customer success planning, value documentation, and renewal readiness.

    • Strengthen the accuracy and detail of customer health and renewal forecasts.

    • Deliver measurable progress against adoption, engagement, and customer outcome goals.

    • Build and execute mitigation plans for at-risk customers.

    • Identify and support qualified expansion opportunities.

    • Become a trusted advisor to customer stakeholders and a reliable source of account intelligence internally.

    In your first 5 months, you’ll:

    • Build a healthy and well-managed portfolio of enterprise customers.

    • Deliver strong retention and renewal performance.

    • Improve adoption and value realisation across complex customer organisations.

    • Develop trusted relationships with senior and executive customer stakeholders.

    • Demonstrate strong forecast accuracy and proactive risk management.

    • Contribute repeatable best practices and insight to Pleo’s broader enterprise Customer Success model.

    • Be recognised as a senior individual contributor capable of managing Pleo’s most important and complex customer relationships.

    Success in this role looks like

    • Enterprise customers have clear success plans connected to measurable business outcomes.

    • Executive and operational customer relationships are strong and multi-threaded.

    • Customer risks are identified early and addressed through structured mitigation plans.

    • Renewal forecasts are detailed, accurate, and supported by clear account evidence.

    • Customers demonstrate stronger product adoption and value realisation.

    • Escalations are managed with urgency, clarity, and strong customer communication.

    • Internal teams are aligned around customer priorities, responsibilities, and next steps.

    • Renewal and retention performance is strong across the assigned portfolio.

    • Expansion opportunities are identified through customer value and business need rather than transactional selling.

    • Pleo is viewed as a strategic partner rather than simply a product provider.

    Candidate profile summary

    The strongest candidate for this role is an experienced enterprise Customer Success professional who combines senior-level relationship skills with commercial awareness, analytical thinking, and disciplined account execution.

    They have at least three years of direct enterprise experience and are comfortable managing complex customers with multiple stakeholders, high expectations, and significant revenue impact.

    They know how to earn executive trust, demonstrate value, predict and prevent churn, maintain accurate forecasts, and mobilise cross-functional teams around customer outcomes. They are proactive, credible, highly organised, and capable of protecting and growing Pleo’s most strategic customer relationships.
